Independently reviewed all 78 exact test call paths after integrating main accf6fc7. Prompt deserialization, block construction, level/request validation, argv and YAML rendering are pure. Manager tests use SessionState, Noop emitter and in-memory channels for accepted/rejected/cancelled/cleared/switched model and provider snapshots; Office has no mentioned scene and memory has no installed database handle, so both return before external access. SDK-effort tests use only private temporary JSON and a non-executed placeholder; cache fingerprint/get/put read filesystem metadata/configuration and access an in-memory map. Claude, Codex, Pi and DSH lifecycle fixtures use fake JSONL peers or temporary Python processes, SessionState, Noop emitters and private transcript files, never real runtimes. The two merged Pi regressions cover resumed route/default-effort changes with same-turn steering and legacy print effort/route arguments. The merged DSH regression records set/clear/omitted effort YAML across three turns while preserving steering. Their cfg(test) seed helper only fingerprints the isolated launch context and populates the metadata cache; PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR/DSH_HOME and the executable/working directory are private temporary paths. Driver resolve_turn reaches inspect only through its cache-hit return and never reaches native run_probe, SDK imports or real model requests. DSH generated codeg-*.patch.yml is excluded from the configuration fingerprint, keeping the seeded cache valid after patch publication. Shared ledger/readiness tests use only in-memory state/channels. Native ACP tests use JSON, SessionState, Notify/Mutex and in-memory duplex reactors; receipt history uses the temporary transcript writer with CODEG_HOME scoped to a private temporary directory. Owned-bootstrap tests use pure environment planning, private temporary files and worker threads, never AppState or a database. Separately reviewed effort Node tests call pure wire checks, mock metadata/selection, read-only temporary settings, per-model default getters and sampling merges with CODEG_PI_EFFORT_PROBE=0; runner apply and SDK probe entry points are excluded. Owned runtime Node/Python tests use fixed source fragments, fake Agents/processes and pure ACP SDK routing, never the full application or SQLite. Recursive resource fingerprinting includes production mjs/cjs/js/py/json, including the three main effort resources, exactly once. ReceiptBatch closes history before successor admission; late acknowledgements remain unconfirmed. No allowlisted call chain creates AppDatabase, SQLite, migrations, seeds, network connections or a real Agent/provider. Real-instance observations and all unlisted suites remain excluded from execution. Regenerate the source fingerprint only after the merged production/test call chains are reviewed and frozen. The runner-only YAML regression constructs an in-memory DshLaunchProfile, calls render_patch_with_options and parses the returned string with serde_yaml; it checks a single two-row runner sequence and a valid zero-row stock sequence. It performs no file I/O or process/runtime/database initialization. The reviewed production fix omits an empty serialized prefix only when a runner sequence follows; ordinary empty stock patches remain []. The preview startup fix changes only the OpenClaw manifest activation.onStartup flag. The 78 Rust test call paths and runtime launch stubs are unchanged; owned-bootstrap tests still write private resource bytes without importing or launching OpenClaw. The added Node audit evaluates only the published startup-selector function in an isolated VM with a memory-plugin predicate stub, not the runtime or SQLite. The preview native-steering diagnostics add only fixed-enum/boolean/elapsed stderr and tracing records, with log failures isolated and 64 readiness records per turn. Production submit, notifications, steering extension, bootstrap source patch and guard order remain unchanged. New observations use own data descriptors without invoking accessors or the upstream session getter. Gateway false responses carry coarse reasons only after exact original owner validation. The 78 Rust call chains are unchanged. The added Node tests use fake Gateway/Agents, controlled promises, a pure VM bootstrap fragment and the published pure ACP SDK router, never an application entry point, SQLite, network, runtime or provider. Production resources were independently reviewed and frozen before regenerating this fingerprint. The final logging sink promotes only OpenClaw stderr with the exact owned prefix, a 2048-byte bound and per-phase field/enum/type/integer whitelists rebuilt as safe JSON. Connection identity comes from the host; conversation observation uses nonblocking try_read. Original stderr tail and debug output remain intact. Existing native capability-test assertions additionally exercise this pure serde_json/std parser with valid and rejected input, including secret fields, spoofed owner, access types, missing fields and oversized records. The 78 test names are unchanged; this added call path performs no file, process, database, network or runtime access. The OpenClaw MCP cleanup compatibility fix changes only owned compat/plugin resources: fixed package/version/export-map and full-source hashes are checked before importing the actual ESM Client/Protocol/OpenClaw stdio classes in production. The non-async Client.close wrapper observes only owned stdio failures and returns the original Promise unchanged, preserving initialize rejection, explicit close rejection, cleanup uncertainty and unrelated transports. Rust tests do not call this loader or start a Gateway; their owned-bootstrap paths only materialize private resource bytes. The new Node regressions read saved audited SDK method fragments and fixture JSON, evaluate them against fake transports in a local VM/Node process, and use temporary package metadata to reject resolver/version/hash drift. They never import a real SDK, Agent, runtime, database or provider. The original 78 Rust test names and their reviewed call chains remain unchanged. The additional same-turn MCP preparation regression evaluates fixed audited OpenClaw catalog/lifecycle/cleanup and SDK method fragments in a VM with in-memory fake process/request boundaries. It uses the owned ACP bridge and Gateway controller with an explicitly synthetic later backend registration; timeout, empty-tool fallback, sticky cleanup uncertainty, owner/session/host/current-token guards and a single B injection are checked without real SDK imports, Agent/model execution, database, network or child-process startup. Both fixture JSON files and all production resources are frozen before computing this fingerprint. The 2026-11-04 OpenClaw preparation change adds 12 independently reviewed exact tests (90 total). They call the production manager ledger/admission/wait/dispatch with SessionState, Noop emitter and private in-memory mpsc/oneshot channels only. ConnectionManager::new constructs memory state and reads the spawn timeout environment; TerminalShellRuntimeConfig::new is an in-memory default. insert_test_connection_live never launches a process. enqueue_cancel is the database-free cancellation admission half; tests never invoke cancel(db) or construct a DatabaseConnection. Synthetic readiness JSON, TurnComplete, map/Arc replacement, command backpressure and Tokio paused time exercise 107-second preparation and 120-second admission budget without real waiting. Injection acknowledgement is produced by a fake command receiver; FeedbackSubmitted only updates memory through the Noop emitter. No AppState, AppDatabase, SQLite including in-memory databases, migrations, seeds, real SDK, Agent, model or network is initialized. New owned Gateway lifecycle resources are materialized as bytes in existing bootstrap tests, not imported into a runtime. Separate Node tests execute pure owned modules and fixed published factory fragments in a VM with explicit in-memory timer/diagnostic stubs. Original 78 tests retain their reviewed boundaries. Production and all 12 added test call chains were reviewed before updating this fingerprint. The final submission logs project only parsed UUID connection identities (or None), never the raw caller string. This formatting-only change adds no I/O or database call path. The two client-message proof tests were independently reviewed on 2026-11-04: they call send_prompt_inner_raw through the existing in-memory Manager/SessionState/Noop/mpsc fixture, pure UUID parsing, TurnComplete state application and serde serialization only. They never enter send_prompt_linked, AppDatabase, an SDK, a child process or a model. They cover exact admitted UUID, busy rejection, successor replacement, inactive omission, absent/non-UUID clearing and empty/closed-channel rejection before proof assignment. The same-host begin test and expanded admitted-turn proof test were independently re-reviewed: OpenClaw admission establishes its host under the same state gate before dequeue, pending capture/query use only the existing in-memory ledger, and repeated begin preserves ready/current/first/retirement state until the host generation changes. No native peer, transcript writer, SDK or database is reached.
Integrated origin/main f9bdbab2237195e196352ea26cee23e7174e30bb on 2026-11-04 after reviewing its three commits. All 19 upstream exact Prompt test names are already included in these 93 reviewed names; no executable test was added or removed. Upstream changes only four project-version metadata values and the WhatsApp turn broker plus its health capability. The WhatsApp broker paths are not reached by these Noop/in-memory Prompt, native steering, driver or owned-bootstrap fixtures. The new negotiated-question fake-broker test remains compile-only because it is outside the reviewed myclaw_prompt set. No AppDatabase, SQLite, migration, seed, network or real Agent/SDK path was added to an allowlisted call chain. Retain the recursively audited production-resource fingerprint algorithm rather than the older upstream three-resource algorithm. Both native_steering_v1 and whatsapp_question_reply_v1 advertise their separate existing protocols; no routing or authentication policy changed. Recompute the fingerprint only after this reviewed merged source is frozen.
2026-11-04 independent merged-source review: all upstream 93 exact test call paths were freshly inspected, not accepted solely from historical review text. Manager/Prompt (16), ACP state/duplex/receipt ordering (9), pure owned/OpenClaw bootstrap plans and private resource files (8), steering ledger/preparation admission (18), and CLI/effort (42) were followed through fixtures and transitive helpers. Manager tests install no DB handle; memory returns before platform access and Office has no mentioned scene. Only enqueue_cancel is exercised, never cancel(db) or send_prompt_linked. Noop state emission has no external subscribers. Native receipt history is ordinary JSONL under a scoped temporary CODEG_HOME; SACP transport tests are in-memory duplex reactors. CLI driver fixtures execute only exact private fake Python scripts or duplex peers; model/provider efforts use the reviewed deterministic metadata-cache seeds and do not reach native probe while the frozen fixture and ancestor package metadata remain unchanged. Production cache-miss fallback still exists; this review does not claim otherwise. All reviewed paths avoid AppDatabase, SQLite including in-memory DB, SQL, migrations, real SDK/Agent/model and network. Execution requires one test thread, a unique 0700 temporary ancestor used for TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP with umask077 and no symlinks, trusted Python/PATH with startup injection variables removed and PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1, plus stable cache fingerprint inputs. Fixed-PID DSH transcript subdirectories are private through that ancestor rather than randomly named fixture roots.
2026-11-04 unified Hermes reasoning delta: independently reviewed four added exact tests (97 total). The two hermes_reasoning tests call only Hermes-scoped snapshot presence/enum validation and strict JSON boolean handshake parsing. The two owned_bootstrap additions call only plan_launch_env over explicit in-memory env lists and path strings, verifying joint markers and native opt-out with reasoning retained; they do not call materialization, codeg_home_dir, prepare_launch_env, ACP initialize, a launcher, SDK or database. The obsolete separate Python launcher and its five layout/materialization tests were removed. Existing owned-bootstrap materialization tests still write supplied literal bytes only inside TempDir; embedding the new Python resource does not import it. Frozen production connection changes validate the snapshot, reuse the original launcher/shared owned bootstrap, and require an initialize handshake; those runtime launch paths are not executed by this Rust whitelist. The separately reviewed 37 Python tests use fake Hermes modules, fixed source-pinned function definitions, in-memory queues/threads and isolated fake Python consoles with scoped HOME/PYTHONPATH; no installed runtime or sqlite3 is imported. The 15 owned Node bootstrap tests use private published-wrapper fixtures, fixed source hashes/public signature checks, fake Python stdio consoles and VM/mocked hooks, not the Hermes application. The eight effort Node tests import owned modules but with CODEG_PI_EFFORT_PROBE=0 call only mock metadata/selection, readonly settings and pure wire/getter/sampling helpers, never SDK/runner entry points. The production resource recursion includes the Hermes Python bridge exactly once and excludes test entry files. The owner completed local Rust formatting and froze the merged production bytes after this call-path review. The final source fingerprint was computed from that reviewed frozen source; earlier fingerprints are not reused.
